description: List customers of the store (paginated), by customer ID ascending by default. updated_from/updated_to filter by last-change time (updated_at) for incremental CRM sync. Sync recipe: updated_from=<cursor>, sort_by=updated_at, sort_direction=asc, then advance the cursor to the largest updated_at seen — a customer that changes mid-paging moves to the end instead of being skipped, and an all=true run cut off at 500 items resumes from that cursor. Both bounds are inclusive, so the boundary customer comes back on the next poll — deduplicate by customer_id. The response carries a machine-readable coverage envelope (coverage, received, total_count, pages_read); coverage:"partial" MUST be reflected in the user-facing answer and forbids claiming the listing is complete.

all.description: Fetch all pages via auto-pagination, up to 500 items; ignores page/per_page.

fields.description: CSV columns; only valid together with format:"csv". Field names are validated against the item schema of the operation's response — an unknown name fails with the list of allowed fields. Default: every top-level scalar field of the item.

format.description: Output format: "csv" renders the items as RFC 4180 CSV (a leading "# coverage:" comment line, then the header row) instead of JSON — cheaper for wide exports. Default: JSON.

per_page.description: Items per page, 1-100 (default 25). Values outside the range are clamped.

redact.description: Use redact:true when the task does not need personal data (e.g. counting or aggregating orders) — personal fields (name, phone, email, date of birth, delivery address and its parts, notes) are replaced with "[redacted]". Applies to the response only; request bodies are never redacted. Default false.

sort_by.description: Sort field (default "customer_id"). Use "updated_at" for incremental sync.

updated_from.description: Earliest customer update time, inclusive. RFC 3339 date-time, e.g. "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z".

updated_to.description: Latest customer update time, inclusive. RFC 3339 date-time, e.g. "2026-10-02T00:00:00Z".
